segments: 70 Chronography of Bar Hebraeus. His cousin (Placidia's son?) he made Caesar,
and sent him to Rome with his mother.
And afterwards he sent him the royal crown;
and Valentinian the Third reigned for thirty-two years.
And Theodosius was constant in fasting and in prayer;
and on Wednesday and Friday he used to fast the evening fast.
And when the bishop of Hebron died,
that king took his tunic while it was dirty,
and put it on so that he might be blessed by it.
At this time Yazdegerd, king of the Persians, died.
And Bahram his son arose after him for twenty-two years.
And peace ceased.
And the Persians armed themselves against the Romans;
and the Romans conquered and took the Persians captive.
And after these things there was peace,
while the persecution of the Christians did not cease in Persia during the whole time of Bahram.
And after the peace, the Persians grew insolent and marched up against Resh'aina;
and they turned back from it in shame.
And again they marched up with great force,
and they were defeated.
And the Romans took seven thousand captives from the region of Arzan (Arzon);
these whom Acacius, bishop of Amida, bought and liberated,
when he sold the cups and platters of gold and silver belonging to the churches.
At this time, the Burgundian people, who lived by carpentry and dwelt in quietness,
when the Huns were taking them captive,
believed and were baptized.
And immediately three thousand of them destroyed ten thousand of the Huns;
and they were confirmed in the faith.
And Theodosius sent for Valentinian, his cousin,
and brought him to Constantinople,
and gave him his daughter Eudoxia as a wife;
and he took her and went to Rome.
And at this time dispute increased between the empires of the Romans and of the Persians because of the persecution of the Christians in Persia.
And also many merchants the king of the Persians wronged,
and seized their goods.
And he hired Christian craftsmen, goldsmiths, whom he defrauded,
and did not give their wages.
And on this account {OCR?: or, on these accounts}, the Romans went down into Armenia, and took captives and plundered;
and they killed seven generals of the Persians,
and the rest drowned in the Euphrates,
especially the Arabs whom they had brought to their aid.
And after these things, there was peace, and the persecution subsided.
However, barbarians came out and took captive from Thrace and Illyricum a great populace.
